turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Howzit, come sit. I'll just do your vitals. Temperature is 37.8, blood pressure 132 over 84, pulse 86.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Shame, not bad hey. We sat at that robot by the mall forever, the N1 was crawling, I thought we'd miss you completely.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Ja, traffic is hectic. My sister had a molar pulled in June and she sat in this same queue moaning the whole morning, proper drama.
[SEG0004] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And he talked Proteas the whole drive. They collapsed again last night.
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, don't start me. That bowling was rubbish. We were going to braai, then loadshedding hit, and the weather guy says it only cools down by Thursday.
[SEG0006] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, err, this screen has frozen on me again. Right. What's brought you in?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Doc, my cheek is swollen and the tooth is throbbing. It's been three days, since they put the crown on.
[SEG0008] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, uh, say that again? I clicked the wrong tab.
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Throbbing toothache, right hand side, and the cheek has blown up. Three days now.
[SEG0010] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The dentist did the crown on Friday and then the rooms shut. He's away till next week, no locum, we phoned.
[SEG0011] person_4 (DOCTOR): When did the pain actually start? Same day as the crown?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, the receptionist said he's in Ballito with his family. The emergency dentist in town is fully booked, we tried twice this morning already.
[SEG0013] person_4 (DOCTOR): I heard that. I asked when the pain started. Friday, or later? Just say it again.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh. Sorry. Friday evening, same day as the crown, the top right one. Three days of this throb.
[SEG0015] person_4 (DOCTOR): Have you felt feverish? Hot, or shivery?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): A bit warm, ja. Mild. Not shivery.
[SEG0017] person_1 (NURSE): Temperature was 37.8 when I checked just now.
[SEG0018] person_4 (DOCTOR): How bad is the throb, out of ten?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): The right one, about a seven. Worse at night, and if I chew on that side. I've been taking two Panados, the 500s, every six hours, and it just takes the edge off.
[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any trouble swallowing, or with your breathing?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Swallowing is fine, breathing is fine.
[SEG0022] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any medicine allergies? Penicillin in particular.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing. I've had penicillin before, no reaction.
[SEG0024] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He takes his blood pressure pill every morning, amlodipine, five milligrams. I pack the pill box.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, high blood pressure, about eight years. That's the only thing. Panados since Friday, no other tablets, and I'm not on blood thinners.
[SEG0026] person_4 (DOCTOR): Eight years, ja, I'm putting that in. Sorry, the cursor jumped. Is it just this tooth, or the others as well?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Just that crowned one, top right. The others are fine, no pain there.

[SEG0028] person_4 (DOCTOR): Let me look. Open for me. Right cheek is swollen and tender when I press, and the gum around that crowned molar is red and puffy. I don't see any pus, and you open the jaw fully.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, it looks fatter in the morning. I was saying, the bakkie's battery nearly packed up, and the cricket was on, but I couldn't even watch.
[SEG0030] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He did the whole innings recap in the waiting room anyway. Bavuma this, Maharaj that. I just wanted a coffee.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): You have to admit that catch was lekker. And it's meant to be cooler by the weekend, if you believe the forecast. Eish.

[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): Mhm. I'm not with the cricket, this note won't save. This is an infection around the tooth that was crowned. The swelling is your body fighting the infection, fluid and immune cells in the tissue, that's why the cheek blows up, it's not the crown moving into your face.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): So if I just wait till the dentist is back, will it settle?

[SEG0034] person_4 (DOCTOR): I wouldn't just wait. I'm prescribing amoxacillin, no, amoxicillin, five hundred milligrams, by mouth, three times a day, for five days. Finish the course even if it feels better.

[SEG0035] person_4 (DOCTOR): And for the pain, ibuprofen 400 milligrams, by mouth, three times a day, with food, for the next few days. Keep the Panado too, just don't go over those two 500s every six hours.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Three times a day, ja. My cousin in Joburg had some green stuff for a tooth and it made him queasy.
[SEG0037] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, the cousin again? Leave it, that's not your medicine. Your script is amoxicillin 500 milligrams, three times a day, five days.
[SEG0038] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And if he starts battling to swallow or breathe?
[SEG0039] person_4 (DOCTOR): Then don't wait for me. If there's difficulty swallowing, trouble breathing, or the swelling climbs toward the eye or the neck, go straight to casualty, any hour.
[SEG0040] person_4 (DOCTOR): Come back and see me on Thursday so I can check the swelling. And please see the dentist the day the rooms open. I'll put a short letter with the script.
[SEG0041] person_1 (NURSE): I'll print the script out front. My little one was on amox last winter for her ear and she hated the chalky taste, so ja, that's my child, not something on your notes.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Ag, we'll manage. Thursday then. If the bakkie starts, I'll be here. Thanks, doc, and sorry about the cricket lecture.
[SEG0043] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sharp. Thursday, and casualty if the breathing or the swallowing changes. I'm going to fight with this computer a bit longer.

spec.situation: Cheek swelling and throbbing toothache for three days after a crown; fever mild; dentist unavailable; doctor prescribes antibiotic, warns about swallowing or breathing difficulty.

traps.happens: The doctor (or nurse) explains a mechanism or a diagnosis in the patient's body ('the voice box is irritated by reflux', 'diabetes dulls the nerves in the feet', 'the swelling is your body fighting infection'). A nurse or caregiver also mentions a fact about THEIR OWN life (their sister, their child, their own illness).
traps.label_rule: Explanations by the doctor are NEVER symptoms, history or social history of the patient; they may only appear as clinical_assessment or counselling if the doctor stated them as such. A nurse's or caregiver's own life facts are not recorded as the patient's. Each symptom's reported_by is the person who really described it.

features: patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.
tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

omissions.text: Ibuprofen was specifically instructed to be taken with food.
The doctor advised the patient to keep taking Panado/paracetamol as well, but not to exceed two 500 mg tablets every 6 hours.
Penicillin allergy was specifically denied: patient said he had taken penicillin before with no reaction.
The patient denied being on blood thinners.
Jaw opening was full on examination; the recorded finding of 'limited jaw opening absent' misses the positive exam statement that he could open the jaw fully.
The follow-up was specifically to come back on Thursday so the doctor could check the swelling.
